properties.chose: (a) leave it undeclared. Anthony 2026-10-21: "go with (a)". The prefixed id '<graph_id>:<id>' the tracked search hands back opens the record with no new argument, and the reply says so; the published tool list stays the same for every design, so a client that pins tool schemas is not broken by a pin added to the design.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-10-21 while building phase 7 PR 2 (cap:search-design-reaches-the-designs-a-hub-tracks).

WHAT THE PERSON SEES TODAY: on a local hub, `get_node` opens a hit from a pinned design's export when given the hit's prefixed id ('<graph_id>:<id>') or `member: "<graph_id>"`. The tracked search's reply and the hub skill say so. But `reflow2 --describe get_node` (and tools/list) does not list `member`, because tools/list declares it only through a hub's address; an agent that learns tools from their schemas alone would not know it can aim a read.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) LEAVE IT UNDECLARED. The prefixed id needs no new argument, and the reply that hands out the id says how to open it. The listing stays byte-identical everywhere.
(b) DECLARE `member` ON EVERY TOOL of a design that pins at least one design by graph_id, served outside a registry, with a description saying it aims READS at a pinned design's committed export (writes are refused). The listing then differs per design, as a hub's address listing already does.
(c) DECLARE IT ONLY ON THE READ TOOLS of such a design.

PUSHBACK: (b) and (c) make the published schema depend on the design's content, which the --call door reads on every call; a stale tool list on a long-lived MCP session would miss a pin added later.
properties.name: A local hub leaves `member` off its tools' published arguments; the prefixed id opens a pinned design's record
properties.rationale: Built what was unambiguous (both routes work and are tested); the listing is a surface choice for the owner. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
